issues.legal_issue: A landlord’s marriage during a pending tenant’s appeal does not by itself extinguish an established bona fide need for release when the need to accommodate family members continues and comparative hardship favors release.
material_facts: The landlord sought release of a rented premises for a bona fide need that included accommodating her parents and grandparents, who were living separately and needed care.
The initial release order was reversed on appeal, and the landlord married while the tenant’s appeal was pending and later lived with her husband elsewhere.
The landlord’s parents and grandparents continued to need accommodation together, and the landlord’s family remained in rented accommodation.
The tenant had another business and could shift the business elsewhere, while the landlord’s family had no other premises in which to accommodate the parents and grandparents.
issues.conclusion: The landlord’s marriage and relocation did not extinguish the continuing bona fide need for the premises. Considering comparative hardship, the Court allowed the appeal, set aside the High Court’s order, and restored the release order.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 21(1)(a) of the Uttar Pradesh Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972, a building may be released when it is bona fide required by the landlord for occupation by the landlord or a member of the landlord’s family. Although rights ordinarily crystallise when proceedings begin, a court may consider subsequent events and mould relief when the original relief has become inappropriate or cannot be granted, doing so would shorten litigation and enable complete justice, and the event is promptly brought to the court’s attention without unfair surprise. The court must assess the effect of later developments on bona fide need and comparative hardship; a natural event such as marriage does not automatically extinguish a continuing need. The Court relied on Om Prakash Gupta v. Ranbir B. Goyal (2002) 2 SCC 256, which discussed Pasupuleti Venkateswarlu v. Motor & General Traders (1975) 1 SCC 770, and was approved in Ram Kumar Barnwal v. Ram Lakhan (2007) 5 SCC 660; it also considered Hasmat Rai v. Raghunath Prasad (1981) 3 SCC 103 and Kedar Nath Agrawal v. Dhanraji Devi (2004) 4 AWC 3709 (SC).

rule.if: landlord_release_proceeding and bona_fide_need_includes_accommodating_family and marriage_occurs_during_pending_appeal and family_accommodation_need_continues_after_marriage and landlord_family_lacks_suitable_accommodation and tenant_can_relocate_business

predicates.landlord_release_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking release of rented premises for the landlord’s bona fide need.
predicates.bona_fide_need_includes_accommodating_fa: The landlord’s asserted need included accommodating family members in the premises.
predicates.marriage_occurs_during_pending_appeal: The landlord married while an appeal concerning the release proceeding was pending.
predicates.family_accommodation_need_continues_afte: After the marriage, the family members whose accommodation formed part of the asserted need still required accommodation together.
predicates.landlord_family_lacks_suitable_accommoda: The landlord’s family had no other suitable premises in which to accommodate those family members.
predicates.tenant_can_relocate_business: The tenant had another business and could move the business conducted in the premises elsewhere.

issues.definition: When a landlord’s need to accommodate family members continues after the landlord marries, the family lacks suitable accommodation, and the tenant can relocate a business, the landlord remains entitled to release.
